title: How early should you arrive at Gatwick Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: A traveller with a backpack looking up at the departures boards in an airport terminal
intro: Two hours before a European flight and three before long-haul is the usual advice for Gatwick, but your terminal, your bags and the time of day all change the sums. Here's how to work out the right time for your flight.
seo_title: Gatwick: how early to arrive, North vs South (2026)
seo_description: About 2 hours before a European flight and 3 before long-haul. Which airlines use North and South, bag drop deadlines, the new liquids rules and busy times.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **European flight, hand luggage only, checked in online:** about 2 hours before departure.
- **European flight with a bag to drop:** 2 to 2.5 hours, more at peak times.
- **Long-haul:** about 3 hours.
- **Early mornings (roughly 5 to 8am) and school holidays:** add 30 minutes or more.

These are the timings most airlines and travel guides suggest for Gatwick. The deadlines that actually matter, for check-in, bag drop and boarding, are set by your airline and shown on your booking. We checked this advice in October 2026; procedures change, so always look at your airline's and [Gatwick's](https://www.gatwickairport.com/) current guidance before you travel.

sections.heading: North or South Terminal?
sections.text:
Gatwick has two terminals, North and South, and going to the wrong one is the most common way to lose time. They're linked by a free shuttle train that takes about two minutes, plus the walk at each end and any wait, so allow 10 to 15 minutes if you get it wrong.

When we checked in October 2026:

- **easyJet**, Gatwick's biggest airline, uses the **North Terminal**.
- **British Airways** uses the **South Terminal**.
- **Wizz Air** and **Jet2** use the **South Terminal**.
- **TUI** uses both, depending on the flight, so check your booking carefully.

Airlines have moved between the terminals several times in recent years, so check your terminal on your booking or the airline's app the day before, especially if you last flew from Gatwick a while ago. Gatwick's railway station is at the South Terminal, so if you're flying from the North, you'll need the shuttle.

sections.heading: Bag drop deadlines
sections.text:
If you're checking a bag, the bag drop deadline is the time to plan around. Airlines are strict, and turning up a few minutes late usually means you can't fly with your bag.

- **Short-haul airlines** typically close bag drop between 40 and 60 minutes before departure.
- **Long-haul airlines** usually close check-in at least 60 minutes before, and some earlier.

Work backwards from that deadline, not from the departure time, and allow for a queue. On a busy summer morning in the North Terminal, the bag drop queue for the first wave of flights can take a long time on its own.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
Gatwick finished installing new CT scanners across all its security lanes in spring 2025. Its own guidance now says liquids no longer need to be in containers of 100ml or less: each container can be up to two litres, and you can usually leave liquids and laptops in your bag. A few things to know:

- **Metal, insulated and double-walled bottles must be empty**, including many reusable water bottles, vacuum flasks and travel mugs.
- **Coats and belts with buckles** still need to come off.
- **Your return airport may have different rules.** Not every airport has the new scanners, so pack for the strictest airport on your trip, or you could lose a bottle of sun cream on the way home.

Security is busiest in the early morning, when lots of holiday flights leave at once, and during school holidays. If you're flying at 6am in August or at the start of half term, Gatwick's paid Fast Track lane can be worth it; on a quiet weekday, you probably won't need it.

sections.heading: How long to allow, worked out
sections.text:
Here's how the timings add up for a few typical trips:

- **City break, hand luggage only, Thursday lunchtime flight:** arrive about 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours before. Allow time to walk to your gate, as some at Gatwick are a long way from security, and gates usually close 20 to 30 minutes before departure.
- **Family holiday, bags to drop, 6.30am flight in August:** arrive about 2.5 to 3 hours before, so around 3.30 to 4am. Bag drop and security are both at their busiest then.
- **Long-haul to [Barbados](/destinations/barbados), [Orlando](/destinations/orlando) or [Dubai](/destinations/dubai):** arrive 3 hours before, more in the school holidays. Make sure passports, visas and any travel authorisation, like the US ESTA, are sorted well before the day.
- **Winter sun to [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) or [Madeira](/destinations/madeira) on a Saturday:** treat it like a busy summer day, about 2.5 hours with bags. Saturday mornings are popular for holiday flights all year.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
Gatwick is one of the easiest London airports to reach by train:

- **Gatwick Express** runs non-stop from London Victoria in about 30 minutes.
- **Southern and Thameslink** trains run from Victoria, London Bridge, Blackfriars, St Pancras and towns across the south east, often for less than the Express. Thameslink can be a good option from north London and Bedfordshire.
- **By car**, Gatwick is just off the M23. Pre-booked parking is much cheaper than turning up, and the drop-off areas outside both terminals charge a fee, so check the current price before you go.

Very early trains are limited, so if you're on a 6am flight, check the first train will get you there in time, or think about a hotel at the airport the night before.

sections.heading: Five ways to make it easier
sections.text:
- **Check in online** as soon as it opens, and save your boarding pass to your phone.
- **Check your terminal** the day before.
- **Travel with hand luggage only** if you can, so you can skip bag drop entirely.
- **Know the liquids rules** for both airports on your trip.
- **Head to the gate when it's called**, not when it says it's closing. Some of Gatwick's gates are a long walk from the departure lounge.

If you haven't picked where you're going yet, our guides to [where to go in winter](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january), [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [beach holidays](/destinations/beach-holidays) are a good place to start. And if you're flying from the north instead, see [how early to arrive at Manchester Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-manchester-airport).

faqs.question: Is 2 hours enough at Gatwick?
faqs.answer: For a European flight with hand luggage only, two hours is usually enough outside peak times. If you're dropping a bag, flying early in the morning or travelling in the school holidays, allow 2.5 hours or more.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Gatwick for an international flight?
faqs.answer: For long-haul flights, arrive about three hours before departure. Check-in and bag drop for long-haul flights usually close at least an hour before take-off, and some airlines close earlier.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get between Gatwick's North and South Terminals?
faqs.answer: The free shuttle train takes about two minutes, but with walking and waiting, allow 10 to 15 minutes. The railway station is at the South Terminal.

faqs.question: Do liquids need to be under 100ml at Gatwick?
faqs.answer: Not any more. Gatwick's new scanners mean containers can be up to two litres, though metal and insulated bottles must be empty. Other airports, including the one you fly home from, may still have the 100ml rule, so check before you pack.
